title: Text can hold bulleted lists
body:
`scene::markup::runs` turns a label's string into `Run`s of one font and color each. `text::layout` breaks the runs into lines at each `\n` and wraps them within `width`, greedily or justified. A list today is written by hand as lines that start with a dash or a bullet character. Their wrapped lines run back to the left edge, and consecutive items sit one line height apart like any other lines.

## Proposal

- In a text's string, a line that starts with `- ` is a bullet item. A line is the start of the string or the text after a `\n`, in a block string too. Markup reads it, so the lexer and the parser stay as they are.
- A literal leading `- ` is written `\-` in markup: `"\\- 5"` in a quoted string, `\- 5` in a block string.
- Each item draws "•" in the text's color and hangs its wrapped lines under its first word. Consecutive items sit a little apart, in proportion to the text size. `width` includes the indent.
- With `text-align justify` each item justifies on its own, and its last line stays left-aligned.
- Lines without `- ` stay plain paragraphs, so a bold heading line can lead the list.
- `text` and a box's text get it in PNG, SVG and PDF alike, since all three take positions from `text::layout`. Text with no `- ` lines does not move.
